extracted_stakeholders.name: Penan
extracted_stakeholders.role: Indigenous tribe living in Sarawak, Borneo, relying on forests for survival.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Malaysian Government
extracted_stakeholders.role: State authority responsible for land rights and development projects.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Sarawak State Government
extracted_stakeholders.role: Local government supporting commercial logging and dam projects.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Logging Companies (Samling, Interhill, Shin Yang)
extracted_stakeholders.role: Companies involved in logging activities in Penan territories.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Survival
extracted_stakeholders.role: Advocacy group supporting Penan rights and opposing harmful projects.

extracted_factors.Label: Deforestation for Logging and Oil Palm Plantations
extracted_factors.Description: Forests are being cleared by logging companies and for oil palm plantations, affecting the Penan's resources and way of life.

extracted_factors.Label: Hydroelectric Dams Construction
extracted_factors.Description: New dams being built in Sarawak flood Penan villages and impact their land rights and independence.

extracted_factors.Label: Loss of Forest Resources
extracted_factors.Description: Deforestation and land use changes lead to the depletion of resources crucial for the Penan's survival.

extracted_factors.Label: Forced Resettlement
extracted_factors.Description: Penan communities are forced to move due to rising waters from dam projects, leading to loss of independence and traditional lifestyle.

extracted_factors.Label: Unrecognized Land Rights
extracted_factors.Description: The lack of legal recognition of Penan land rights enables unrestricted development projects on their lands.
